title: Harden org join workflow with dynamic email rules, domain attestation, and RBAC v2 compatibility
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: We currently rely on a static domain allowlist/denylist which is brittle for large partners and lacks contextual rules for transient domains (eg. contractors, temporary test domains). Additionally, RBAC v2 rollout introduces new admin role assertions which must be validated at invite-time to avoid privilege escalation. This ticket designs and implements a hardened org/team join workflow that combines: 1) dynamic email rules with reputation heuristics, 2) domain attestation (DNS TXT + MX heuristics + owner confirmation), 3) SAML mapping checks for account claims, and 4) audit log augmentation for every invite/join decision.

Scope: backend invite policy engine, API contract changes, admin console toggles, and audit schema. This does NOT include full UI redesign for Invite flows (small admin toggles only); follow-up epic will cover self-serve bulk onboarding UI.

Goals and constraints: preserve sub-second path for known good domains, tolerate DNS propagation delays during attestation (grace window), support canary rollout for dedicated customers, ensure no regression to existing invite flows when feature flag disabled, and keep audit logs queryable by customer/org_id and by policy_decision in the last 90 days.
acceptance_criteria: New invite policy engine accepts a JSON policy with allowlist/denylist and dynamic rules and returns deterministic decision with reason_code
Domain attestation flow supports DNS TXT verification and MX fallback and is idempotent within 24 hours
RBAC v2 role assertions are validated at invite acceptance and misaligned SAML assertions are rejected with clear audit entries
Audit logs include fields: timestamp, org_id, actor_id, target_email, decision, reason_code, policy_id, resolution_actions, and upstream_saml_claims
Feature gated behind feature flag 'dynamic_invite_rules' with default off; rollout to 10% of orgs then to 100% after metrics verification
Performance: median invite decision latency < 120ms on warm path; < 500ms for paths requiring remote DNS checks (async path allowed)
Automated tests covering at least: static allowlist, denylist, dynamic rule matching, domain attestation success/failure, RBAC v2 mismatch scenarios

audit_schema_changes: Add invite_events.reason_code (string) - e.g., ALLOW_STATIC, DENY_DYNAMIC_REPUTATION, PENDING_ATTESTATION, SAML_MISMATCH
Add invite_events.policy_id (string) - reference to policy applied
Add invite_events.upstream_saml_claims (string) - serialized minimal claim set for debugging
Add invite_events.resolution_actions (string) - e.g., AUTO_ALLOW, QUEUE_FOR_MANUAL_REVIEW, DENY_AND_BLOCK
db_migrations: Create invite_policies table (id, org_id, name, json_policy, created_at, updated_at)
Add columns to invite_events: policy_id, reason_code, resolution_actions, upstream_saml_claims
Backfill plan: run backfill for last 90 days of invites to set policy_id=legacy-default and reason_code=LEGACY
saml_mapping_notes: When SAML assertion includes 'role' claim map to RBAC v2 role_id. If mapping absent and org has strict_saml_mode=true, reject invite and emit SAML_MISMATCH. For OIDC flows, fall back to email domain matching. Document mapping UI in follow-up ticket.
rollout_plan: Deploy backend with feature flag and migration in a single deploy window
Enable for internal orgs and Redwood test tenants (smoke)
Canary: enable for 10% of eligible orgs for 72 hours, monitor invite latency, false positive/negative rates, and manual review queue size
Full gradual enable after metrics OK; monitor for 14 days then remove feature flag gating
monitoring_dashboards: Domain Attestations - success/failure with latency buckets
